requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Discuss with your counselor the safety equipment, tools, and clothing used while checking or repairing farm equipment. Use this equipment, tools, and/or clothing (when needed or called for) in meeting the requirements for this merit badge. (b) Draw a plan showing a well-equipped farm shop. Point out the shop's mandatory safety devices and features. (c) Find all the universal warning and safety symbols on a piece of equipment and explain what they mean. (d) Describe what a safety data sheet (SDS) is and tell why it is used. Obtain the SDS for any engine coolant, oil, grease, fuel, hydraulic or transmission fluid, or other flammable or hazardous materials you use in meeting the requirements for this merit badge.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: While inspecting a tractor and rotary mower attachment for Farm Mechanics Requirement 1, which safety rules apply to the Power Take-Off (PTO) shaft, Rollover Protective Structure (ROPS), and hydraulic lines?
quiz_item.question: While inspecting a tractor and rotary mower attachment for Farm Mechanics Requirement 1, which safety rules apply to the Power Take-Off (PTO) shaft, Rollover Protective Structure (ROPS), and hydraulic lines?
options: A. Remove the plastic PTO master shield for easier greasing, step across the spinning shaft while the engine is at full throttle, and leave the seatbelt unbuckled with a ROPS frame.
B. Search for pinhole leaks in high-pressure hydraulic hoses by running your bare fingertips along the pressurized hose while a helper works the control lever.

C. Keep all PTO master shields and driveline guards securely in place, disengage the PTO, shut off the engine, and pocket the ignition key before servicing implements, wear the seatbelt whenever ROPS is installed, and use a piece of cardboard or wood (never bare skin) to check for pinhole hydraulic leaks.
D. Prop up a raised front-end loader bucket with a hollow brick and crawl underneath without installing cylinder safety stops.
